pages.text: The anomaly is dosed in n fractions of D. Each fraction kills a fraction exp(−αD − βD²) of its 10⁹ clonogenic cells (α = 0.3 Gy⁻¹, β = 0.03 Gy⁻²); it is resolved when none survives, with probability TCP = exp(−N₀·e^{−n(αD + βD²)}). The normal tissue around it repairs between fractions, but its damage grows as BED = nD(1 + D/3): small fractions spare it, large ones do not.
$(thing)Set$(): Dose per fraction D, Fractions n.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The anomaly's sensitivity α wanders by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The anomaly survives: too many of its clonogens are left; The dose is destroying the normal tissue around the anomaly; The resolution fields are overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The surer the resolution, the faster the work goes.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sensitivity α: α = 0.3·(1 + 0.05·d)$(br)Log cell kill: ln(1/S) = n(αD + βD²)$(br)Resolution probability TCP: TCP = exp(−N₀·e^{−n(αD + βD²)})$(br)Normal-tissue BED: BED₃ = nD(1 + D/3)
